`<query sql="SELECT … " as="rows">…</query>` runs the SQL and stores the rows as `rows` (a single row also as `rows.<column>`); the body renders with them. Shorthand: `<query from="events" pick="id,title" where="city = {{param_city}}" sort="starts_at desc" limit="20" as="rows">`, and `owned="true"` for the viewer's own rows. `cache="5m"` caches per viewer access class; `mock="5"` renders fake rows instead of running the query. With `sql=` it works before the table exists; with `from=` the table must already exist (an unknown table stops the page with a 500, logged as `query from="widgets": unknown table`).

Template values in `sql=` and `where=` are bound as SQL arguments, never spliced into the text: `{{param_city}}` in code becomes `?` (an empty value binds NULL), `'%{{param_q}}%'` inside a literal becomes a concatenation, and `:current_user` binds the viewer's id (NULL when signed out). An optional filter: `WHERE ({{param_city}} IS NULL OR city = {{param_city}})`.

A key that names no page value stops the page with a 500 and the request id (dev mode and a signed-in app admin see `query: nothing binds {{id}}`). URL values are `{{param_<name>}}`, never `{{<name>}}`. Values a request may lack bind NULL instead: `{{param_<name>}}`, the identity values above, `{{aggregate.<name>}}`, and `{{user.<column>}}` for an anonymous viewer (a column the users table lacks is an error for a signed-in viewer).
Tags run innermost first, so a nested <query> runs before the tag around it and cannot read its rows; join the tables in one statement instead. Don't read one tag's result in another tag's SQL.
A failed tag (bad SQL, the deadline, an unbindable value, an unknown shorthand column) stops the page; see api({at:'frontend'}) query_tags for the error, cache and masking rules.
